proposals.evidence: Ordered female + child components, comparing the contracted Tamil formation. Sri Lanka Educational Publications Department, Tamil11, printed p.115 (https://noolaham.net/project/795/79443/79443.pdf), visually verified, explicitly pairs pompiḷai with peṇpiḷḷai in its colloquial/standard table. DEDR4395 supplies peṇ female and4198 piḷḷai child. Survey contractions preserve these components; source vowel/rhotic variants remain unchanged, and borrowing versus shared formation across varieties is not resolved by this component analysis. See tamil-contracted-kinship-evidence.md.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3682 explicitly gives Tamil niṟaiya abundantly/plentifully, Malayalam niṟa fullness and Kannada neṟe fullness/completeness. These surveyed niraya/neriya-type many responses are comparative quantity uses of that documented fullness family. Minority lects absent from the article and possible local Tamil transmission remain subject to review; no literal attestation for those lects is claimed. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

These selected simple survey kiṭṭa/kiṭṭe responses are comparative extensions to that family; DEDR does not print each surveyed lect, and shared regional usage does not by itself exclude contact. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2248 gives Tamil/Malayalam kōḻi fowl, Kota kōy, Kodagu kōḷi, Kannada kōḻi and Tulu kōri/kōḷi. These southern survey kōyi/koyɨ/kōḷi/kośi/kojī-type responses are comparative lect extensions, retaining the glide, lateral and palatal/sibilant variants. The source chicken sense is compatible with fowl; this does not merge them with the distinct central-Dravidian kor family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4798 gives Tamil/Malayalam māṭu ox and Kota māṛ beast, explicitly including cattle and buffalo. The southern survey maḍɨ/maḍu cow responses are comparative lect extensions of this cattle term, with a more specific female-bovine elicitation gloss than the Tamil/Malayalam ox gloss. Preserve that semantic difference and all original vowel-length/voicing notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
